subject: Medford High School Project Next Steps
overview: The Council approved a joint press release and timeline for the Medford High School project, focusing on cost-mitigation strategies for the estimated $700 million renovation. The body also addressed municipal infrastructure funding, zoning amendments for vacant properties, and the operational status of the city's ambulance and veteran services.

items.title: Ceremonial recognitions and records
items.summary: The Council honored veterans, recognized the outgoing Veteran Services Director, and approved records of several special and regular meetings from October and November 2026.

items.title: Winter aid and preparedness
items.summary: Approved a resolution inviting residents to participate in upcoming winter aid events, including clothing giveaways and heating assistance clinics.

items.title: Public Works report on private ways
items.summary: Approved the Public Works and Facilities Committee report regarding legal liability for snow plowing and a request for better website information on private way maintenance.

items.title: National Grid gas main replacement
items.summary: Approved a grant of location for National Grid to replace 1,665 feet of gas main along Fulton Street and Brogan Road subject to conditions on abutter communication and paving quality.

items.title: Vacant property zoning amendment
items.summary: Approved an amendment to the zoning ordinance deleting the section on vacant and foreclosing properties, effective concurrently with the implementation of a new general ordinance in August 2027.

items.title: Veteran Services staffing update
items.summary: Approved a request for an update on the Veterans Department vacancy; the Chief of Staff reported that the office is currently staffed by an acting director while interviews for a permanent replacement begin next week.

items.title: Medford High School project communication
items.summary: Approved a joint press release outlining the timeline for finalized taxpayer impact data, which will be presented at a joint meeting on February 2, 2027. Discussion emphasized strategies to mitigate the impact of the multi-hundred million dollar project through pension funding shifts and new growth revenue.

items.title: Cataldo Ambulance Service sale inquiry
items.summary: Approved a resolution seeking a legal analysis of the city's ambulance contract following reports of a potential sale; owner Dennis Cataldo testified that there is no imminent sale and recent filings were procedural.

items.title: Municipal and public safety appropriations
items.summary: Approved appropriations including $35,000 for a police chief search consultant, $85,000 for a recreation center feasibility study, and various sums for fire headquarters repairs and flood mitigation.

items.title: Law Department supplemental appropriation
items.summary: Tabled a request for a $269,295 supplemental appropriation for the Law Department to allow for further discussion on alternative funding and a requested audit.

items.title: Fire Department drone policy
items.summary: Referred the Medford Fire Department’s unmanned aerial system policy and surveillance impact report to the Public Health and Community Safety Committee.

items.title: Traffic safety petition on Sturgis Street
items.summary: Heard a resident petition regarding speeding and one-way violations on Sturgis Street; the council recommended a walking audit with traffic engineers to assess physical calming measures.
